planting.note: Grow in a hanging basket or on a slim moss pole in bright, indirect light; this is the lance-leaved counterpart to the rounder 'Wide Form' sold under the same species name.

directions: This is the slender, elongated-leaf trade form of the swiss cheese vine, distinguished from the rounder 'Wide Form' by a lance-shaped blade roughly twice as long as it is wide and by smaller, more tightly packed perforations. Foliage stays thinner in texture and the internodes run shorter, giving a denser, wirier climb than the broad-leaved form when trained upward on a pole. Left untrained it trails and cascades nicely from a hanging basket, though fenestrations stay smaller and less numerous without a climbing surface to trigger mature leaf development. Keep it warm, humid, and in a chunky aroid mix that dries slightly between waterings, and rotate the pot occasionally so growth doesn't lean permanently toward the light.

common_name: Marble Fantasy Monstera (Tissue-Cultured Variegated Monkey Mask)

planting.note: Grow in bright, indirect light in a chunky, fast-draining aroid mix; this tissue-cultured mericlone shows finer, more stable variegation than the older sectoral 'Variegata' cutting-grown line.

directions: Marble Fantasy is a lab-propagated (tissue-cultured) selection of the fenestrated swiss cheese vine whose leaves carry a fine, marbled speckling of cream and pale green rather than the large, solid-white sectors typical of the older cutting-propagated 'Variegata' line. Because the variegation arises as a stable mericlone rather than a chimeric sport, plants tend to hold a more consistent pattern from leaf to leaf, though individual growers still see some variation in intensity between specimens from different labs. Give it slightly brighter indirect light than a plain green adansonii to fuel the reduced-chlorophyll tissue, but keep it out of direct sun, which scorches the pale patches quickly. Growth is noticeably slower than the species type, so hold off on heavy fertilizing until the root system fills its pot, and provide a light moss pole once vines lengthen to encourage bigger, more fenestrated leaves.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant on a moss pole or totem in bright, indirect light; this golden color form needs more light than plain-green siltepecana to hold its pigment without scorching.

directions: This color form of the silver monstera trades the species' characteristic gray-blue metallic sheen for a warm chartreuse-to-yellow leaf tone that intensifies under bright, filtered light and fades toward green in lower light. It shares the same dramatic heterophylly as the wild-type plant, producing small silvery-gold, elongated juvenile leaves in trailing form and much larger, fenestrated adult leaves once trained up a mossy support. Because the yellow pigmentation reduces chlorophyll density somewhat compared to the standard form, growth runs a touch slower and the plant benefits from slightly warmer, more humid conditions to keep new leaves from emerging pale or crinkled. Let the chunky, well-drained mix dry slightly between waterings and avoid direct sun, which can bleach or scorch the golden foliage.
